close_reason: WONTFIX. Workspace Cargo.toml already declares license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0" at the workspace level (Cargo.toml:34); every crate inherits via license.workspace = true. The TOML metadata is sufficient for crates.io and cargo deny. Adding LICENSE-MIT / LICENSE-APACHE files is unwanted — this convention is intentional. Recorded in AGENTS.md (Conventions and Key Rules sections) so future contributors do not re-file this.
description:
Workspace declares `license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"` (dual license). Convention for dual-licensed Rust crates is to ship both LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE text files inside each crate. Only `crate-jmap-types/LICENSE` exists (and is a single file, not the dual pair).

Affected: all 24 other crates (every crate-jmap-*/ except crate-jmap-types).

crates.io accepts the SPDX identifier and will publish without LICENSE files, so this is not a hard publish blocker. But:
- `cargo package --list` typically emits a warning when LICENSE files are absent for SPDX-only declarations
- License text not bundled inside the crate tarball means downstream auditors / SBOM tools have to look elsewhere
- Most established RustCrypto / tokio-rs / serde-rs crates ship both files

Action: add LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE (canonical text from https://spdx.org/licenses/) to each crate. Optionally, also update `crate-jmap-types/LICENSE` to the canonical pair.

Mark is the open-source-licensing expert per AGENTS.md, so confirm with him before bulk-applying.
title: P2: 24 of 25 crates missing LICENSE-MIT/LICENSE-APACHE files
